I think it's importantly, you know, I'd presume you'd ask, are there others like this in inventory? Absolutely not.
We don't -- this is a large project endeavor that we've been working on and, and didn't reach resolution that got to our hurdle rates, and so stopped the project.
Brennan Hawken
Analyst, UBS
Okay. Did something happen in the, you know, sort of like revenue opportunity that diminished it versus where you planned? Because I'm sure you guys went through the process before you, you know, broke ground, so to speak, at least metaphorically. Or was it that it was really pricey? You know, it turned out to be more expensive to build. Was it the expense side that hurt the, the outlook versus plan, or was it the revenue opportunity?
Jason Tyler
President, Wealth Management, Northern Trust Corporation
Yeah, it was more costly to build than we thought, and the revenue dynamics were not, at that point, going to get to our hurdle rate. And this really is reflective of us taking an extremely disciplined approach on items like this, where we're not going to devote resources to areas where we're not going to achieve our hurdle rate. And so, you know, well, before we talked about this, even internally, one of the pillars that we talked about for the productivity office was looking at our internal investments, and this fits squarely in one of those areas. We define that as areas where we're allocating resources, whether it's capital or expense dollars, and we're not at our hurdle rate.
This is one where we were disciplined in saying, "We're going to stop now, halt it, and not invest more into this.
Brennan Hawken
Analyst, UBS
Yeah. Thanks for explaining that, Jason. It's actually a lot more encouraging than that I interpreted it on paper. So thanks for the color.
Jason Tyler
President, Wealth Management, Northern Trust Corporation
Oh, yeah. No, thanks for asking. It's probably, if it's helpful to you to clarify, it's helpful to others, so thank you.

Jason Tyler
President, Wealth Management, Northern Trust Corporation
Morning, Rob.
Robert Wildhack
Director, Equity Research Analyst, Autonomous Research

Jason Tyler
President, Wealth Management, Northern Trust Corporation

But it is an important part of our financial model to be in that range. And so it's the first thing, it's the first thing I look at, is where are we?

Robert Wildhack
Director, Equity Research Analyst, Autonomous Research

On the expense side, you're going to have the impact from inflation, and to some extent, you know, currency. So you try to focus on what you can control the most, which are those two items, organic growth on fees and organic growth on expenses, to ultimately drive it to the target range.
Michael Brown
Equity Research Analyst, KBW
Okay, thank you both.
Michael O'Grady
Chairman and CEO, Northern Trust Corporation
Sure.
Operator
Betsy Graseck from Morgan Stanley is next. Please go ahead.
Jason Tyler
President, Wealth Management, Northern Trust Corporation
Morning, Betsy.
Connell Schmitz
Equity Research, Morgan Stanley
Hi, good morning. This is actually Connell Schmitz filling in for Betsy.
Jason Tyler
President, Wealth Management, Northern Trust Corporation
How are you?

Jason Tyler
President, Wealth Management, Northern Trust Corporation

Connell Schmitz
Equity Research, Morgan Stanley

Jason Tyler
President, Wealth Management, Northern Trust Corporation
Sure.
Connell Schmitz
Equity Research, Morgan Stanley

Jason Tyler
President, Wealth Management, Northern Trust Corporation
Uh, sure.
Connell Schmitz
Equity Research, Morgan Stanley
To protect NII? Yeah.
Jason Tyler
President, Wealth Management, Northern Trust Corporation
Yep, absolutely. So the duration of the securities book is at 2.1, the duration of the balance sheet is just under 1. At this point with the yield curve, we are talking about where to go from here, and that's not indicating it's going to go up, but it's not on a...

Connell Schmitz
Equity Research, Morgan Stanley
Okay. And then, I guess one follow-up on that same topic. How should we think about earning asset growth in the context of deposit outflows? Potentially, should those flow out on a one-to-one basis, or will you maintain certain balance sheet size, or?
Jason Tyler
President, Wealth Management, Northern Trust Corporation
Yeah. As the deposits come down, the securities can act as, obviously, a funding mechanism for it. That doesn't move very quickly, and so the deposit size is always going to influence the earning asset size. And so what we have to then think about, the constraining factor at that point becomes: What does leverage look like? And we've got a lot of room from a leverage perspective, and so that's what sometimes will lead us to think about discretionary leveraging, just to make sure that we're not missing opportunities to pick up some NII, even if it's a very thin NIM, based on where the size of the balance sheet is, because it doesn't flex super quickly.
Connell Schmitz
Equity Research, Morgan Stanley
Got it. Okay, that's helpful. All right.
Jason Tyler
President, Wealth Management, Northern Trust Corporation
Sure.
Connell Schmitz
Equity Research, Morgan Stanley
That was it from me. Thanks a lot.
Jason Tyler
President, Wealth Management, Northern Trust Corporation
Thank you. Sure.

President, Wealth Management, Northern Trust Corporation
Morning, Mike.

Equity Research Analyst, KBW

Jason Tyler
President, Wealth Management, Northern Trust Corporation
... President, Wealth Management, Northern Trust Corporation

Michael Brown
Equity Research Analyst, KBW
Okay. Thank you for the color.
Jason Tyler
President, Wealth Management, Northern Trust Corporation

Gerard Cassidy
Managing Director, Head of U.S. Bank Equity Strategy and Large Cap Bank Analyst, RBC Capital Markets
Got it. Okay, thank you.
Jason Tyler

Mark Bette
Director of Investor Relations, Northern Trust Corporation
Thank you, Jennifer. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Northern Trust Corporation's Q1 2022 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on our call this morning are Michael O'Grady, our Chairman and CEO, Jason Tyler, our Chief Financial Officer, Lauren Allnutt, our Controller, and Briar Rose from our Investor Relations team. Our Q1 earnings press release and financial trends report are both available on our website at northerntrust.com. Also, on our website, you will find our quarterly earnings review presentation, which we will use to guide today's conference call. This 26 October call is being webcast live on northerntrust.com. The only authorized rebroadcast of this call is the replay that will be made available on our website through 24 May. Northern Trust disclaims any continuing accuracy of the information provided in this call after today.
Please refer to our safe harbor statement regarding forward-looking statements on page 11 of the accompanying presentation, which will apply to our commentary on this call. During today's question and answer session, please limit your initial query to one question and one related follow-up. This will allow us to move through the queue and enable as many people as possible the opportunity to ask questions as time permits. Thank you again for joining us today. Let me turn the call over to Michael O'Grady.
Michael Gerard O'Grady
Chairman and CEO, Northern Trust Corporation
Thank you, Mark. Let me join in welcoming you to our Q1 2022 earnings call. I hope you and your families are healthy and well. Like so many around the world, we at Northern Trust are deeply concerned by the tragic events unfolding in Ukraine. Our hearts go out to the Ukrainian people. Northern Trust has made contributions to humanitarian relief efforts and has matched contributions from our employees to maximize our impact. While we have minimal direct exposure, the crisis brings unique challenges. The broad use of economic sanctions and market restrictions means that we, along with our peers and counterparties, have been called upon to play a role in implementing the world's response. The crisis has added to the uncertainty in the current environment, including volatile markets, supply chain constraints, and persistently high inflation.
Operator
While we are navigating this challenging backdrop, our performance in the quarter generated a 9% increase in revenue compared to the prior year and a return on average common equity of 14.2%. Revenue growth reflected organic growth across each of our businesses, as well as the impact of rising interest rates. Compared to the prior year, our results generated approximately 2 points of positive fee operating leverage and 1 point of positive total operating leverage. We continue to have success executing on our growth strategies across each of our businesses while enhancing our foundational strength through advancements in our data and digital efforts.
